cards.back: Amount of substance containing 6.02 × 10²³ particles (Avogadro's constant). Bridges the atomic scale and grams.
Moles = mass (g) ÷ molar mass (g/mol). The workhorse of every stoichiometry calculation.
Moles = concentration (mol/dm³) × volume (dm³). V in cm³ must be divided by 1000 first.
PV = nRT with R = 8.31 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹. Pressure in Pa, volume in m³ (dm³ ÷ 1000), T in kelvin.
Empirical = simplest whole-number ratio; molecular = actual numbers = (empirical)ₙ. From % mass → moles → divide by smallest.
Reactant fully consumed first — it caps the maximum product. Compare moles ÷ coefficient for each reactant.
actual yield / theoretical yield × 100. Above 100% means impure product.
22.7 dm³/mol (first assessment 2025 data booklet). Older books say 22.4 — use the booklet value.
Same protons, different neutrons: identical chemistry, different mass. Mass spectrometry gives masses + abundances → relative atomic mass.

cards.front: How many atoms in 1.0 mol of H₂O?
cards.back: 3 mol atoms (2 H + 1 O) = 3 × 6.02×10²³ = 1.81×10²⁴ atoms. Count atoms per formula unit before multiplying.

cards.front: Why do 0.5 mol of CO₂ and 0.5 mol of SO₂ contain the same number of molecules but different masses?
cards.back: Same moles = same molecule count (Avogadro). Different molar masses (44 vs 64 g/mol) → different masses. Moles ≠ mass.

cards.front: Formula of a hydrated salt — what's the classic trap?
cards.back: Forgetting the waters of crystallisation: CuSO₄·5H₂O = 159.6 + 90 = 249.6 g/mol. Add the 5H₂O mass.
c₁V₁ = c₂V₂. Every ×10 dilution adds exactly 1 to the pH of an acid.

cards.front: Two reactants given — which is limiting?
cards.back: Convert both to moles, divide each by its coefficient, the smaller result limits. Then scale products from that reagent only.
Reach a conclusion from the information given through logical reasoning — e.g. identify the gas from its molar mass, or the metal from successive ionization energies.

cards.front: Top three stoichiometry traps in Paper 1A?
cards.back: 1) cm³ → dm³ conversions; 2) counting atoms per formula unit (Al₂(SO₄)₃ has 12 O); 3) forgetting waters of crystallisation.
Equal volumes of gases at the same T and P contain equal numbers of molecules — gas volume ratios = mole ratios in equations.
n(NaOH) = cV → n(acid) = ½ n(NaOH) → M = m/n. The equation ratio halves the base moles — always apply it.
Weighted mean mass of an element's isotopes vs 1/12 of carbon-12. Isotopic masses × abundances, summed.
